alternatives: Plasma exchange as an alternative to IVIG
Second-line agents: rituximab 375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 doses, or cyclophosphamide
contraindications: No absolute contraindication to acyclovir, methylprednisolone or IVIG with the current medication list.
Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists (class warning): severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions are reported in autoimmune encephalitis.
output.formulary_status: Methylprednisolone and acyclovir on formulary. IVIG requires pharmacy authorization.
interactions: Methylprednisolone + aspirin: additive gastrointestinal bleeding risk; consider proton-pump inhibitor prophylaxis.
Methylprednisolone + lisinopril: corticosteroid sodium and fluid retention may blunt the antihypertensive effect; monitor blood pressure.
Methylprednisolone in type 2 diabetes: high-dose corticosteroids cause hyperglycemia; capillary glucose monitoring every 4 to 6 hours, insulin correction as needed.
IVIG with coronary artery disease: IVIG carries a thromboembolic risk; ensure hydration and use a slow infusion rate.
Acyclovir + lisinopril: risk of acute kidney injury with volume depletion; maintain hydration and monitor creatinine.
Levetiracetam, atorvastatin, metoprolol, tamsulosin: no clinically significant interaction with acyclovir, methylprednisolone or IVIG.
output.proposed: IV acyclovir; IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days
warnings: Screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before rituximab.
IVIG: monitor creatinine and urine output; headache and aseptic meningitis can occur.
Levetiracetam: irritability, aggression and psychotic symptoms are recognized adverse effects; review dose and indication if behavior changes.

output.query: post-herpes simplex virus autoimmune encephalitis anti-NMDAR antibodies

results.finding: 27% of patients with HSV encephalitis developed autoimmune encephalitis, 64% of them with NMDAR antibodies, typically within about 2 months; children under 4 years presented mainly with choreoathetosis and decreased consciousness, older children and adults mainly with behavioral and cognitive change.
results.source: Armangue T et al. Lancet Neurol 2018;17:760-772

results.finding: NMDAR antibodies of IgG, IgA or IgM class were detected in a proportion of patients with HSV encephalitis, supporting an antibody-mediated mechanism for some post-HSV relapses.
results.source: Pruss H et al. Ann Neurol 2012;72:902-911

results.finding: In HSV-induced anti-NMDAR encephalitis, children presented mostly with choreoathetosis and adults mostly with psychiatric symptoms; most patients received immunotherapy.
results.source: Nosadini M et al. Dev Med Child Neurol 2017;59:796-805

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included, after reasonable exclusion of other disorders.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

output.summary: Published cohort data on autoimmune encephalitis after HSV encephalitis: it follows HSV encephalitis in about a quarter of patients, usually with NMDAR antibodies, with different presentations in young children and in older children and adults.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:10), read with the CSF; sodium 131 mEq/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies, neuronal-surface and onconeural panels negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain serum work-up: blood counts, metabolic panel, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibody panels, and a cell-based serum IgG anti-GluN1 assay read with the CSF
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, thyroid, infectious and paraneoplastic mimics in a 63-year-old former smoker; the serum anti-GluN1 result is read with the CSF, never alone.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Chronic left frontotemporal encephalomalacia and right frontal gliosis unchanged from prior studies; no new lesion, restricted diffusion, enhancement or hemorrhage
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI, compared with the prior studies, to exclude HSV relapse and new structural lesions; residual post-HSV damage neither confirms nor excludes anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: New seizures and behavioral change 2 months after HSV encephalitis need imaging for the new necrotic lesions, enhancement or hemorrhage of HSV relapse before LP; MRI is normal or non-specific in most anti-NMDAR encephalitis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: HSV-1/2 PCR not detected; 8 lymphocytic cells/uL, protein 52 mg/dL, CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands, IgG index 0.78; CSF anti-GluN1 IgG positive 1:32
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, OCB/IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay interpreted in parallel with serum
action_criteria.rationale: CSF HSV PCR separates HSV relapse from post-HSV autoimmune encephalitis, and the CSF cell-based anti-GluN1 assay is the decisive antibody test.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse slowing with left hemispheric predominance, FIRDA and rare left anterior temporal sharp waves; no extreme delta brush or seizure on the routine recording
action_criteria.label: Obtain EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, explicitly assessing for extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: A focal motor seizure with fluctuating responsiveness needs an EEG for seizures, encephalopathic slowing and extreme delta brush.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No thoracic, abdominal or pelvic tumor or lymphadenopathy on contrast CT
action_criteria.label: Perform contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis for an occult tumor in this 63-year-old former smoker
action_criteria.rationale: Patients aged 45 or more with anti-NMDAR encephalitis have fewer teratomas and more carcinomas, and he has 20 pack-years; post-HSV disease is not tumor-associated, so a negative CT ends the routine search.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous ICU EEG for fluctuating responsiveness and catatonic-like staring after a focal seizure, when the routine EEG captured no event
action_criteria.rationale: Episodes of staring and unresponsiveness may be non-convulsive seizures, which only prolonged recording detects.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Glucose, renal and thrombotic monitoring needs; no prohibitive interaction
action_criteria.label: Check interactions of acyclovir, high-dose methylprednisolone and IVIG with aspirin, lisinopril, metoprolol and levetiracetam, given diabetes and coronary artery disease
action_criteria.rationale: Steroid hyperglycemia, IVIG thrombotic risk and acyclovir renal risk with an ACE inhibitor need monitoring here; none changes the choice of therapy.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on post-HSV autoimmune encephalitis
action_criteria.label: Optional: review published evidence on autoimmune encephalitis after HSV encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; no clinical decision in this case depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1 to 2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
Do not attribute the relapse to residual HSV damage or treat it with antivirals alone once CSF HSV PCR is negative: post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis is immune-mediated and needs immunotherapy.
required_recommendations: Restart IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours, with hydration, until CSF HSV PCR excludes HSV relapse, then stop.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges), with capillary glucose monitoring for his diabetes and hydration with a slow IVIG infusion rate given his coronary artery disease.
No further tumor imaging is needed: contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis shows no tumor, and post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis is not tumor-associated.

Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication: he is on levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, which can itself worsen irritability and aggression, so add or switch to lacosamide rather than escalating levetiracetam; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.

Admit to the ICU / neurocritical care for autonomic instability (labile systolic blood pressure 100-170 mmHg with diaphoresis and tachycardia to the 120s) and seizures, with airway assessment and cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m2 weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation, insomnia and catatonic features with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.

Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology; a one-week illness with seizures, dyskinesias and dysautonomia after HSV encephalitis is not a neurodegenerative presentation, and his mother's late-onset Alzheimer disease does not change that.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role here: the cogwheel-like rigidity, orofacial dyskinesias and choreiform movements appeared within a week with the encephalopathy and are not a degenerative parkinsonism.

accepted: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, post-herpes simplex virus (post-HSV autoimmune encephalitis)

differential.key_features: CSF HSV-1/2 PCR not detected; MRI shows only chronic encephalomalacia and gliosis unchanged from prior studies, without new restricted diffusion, enhancement or hemorrhage; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Post-encephalitic structural epilepsy with postictal behavioral change
differential.key_features: The focal seizure fits the left frontotemporal scar, but a week of paranoia and aggression, orofacial and choreiform dyskinesias, dysautonomia and CSF anti-GluN1 IgG are not explained by it.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA or DPPX) or paraneoplastic encephalitis
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX), onconeural antibodies negative and no tumor on CT.
Levetiracetam taken at a stable dose for 2 months with a therapeutic level; it does not cause dyskinesias, dysautonomia, CSF pleocytosis or CSF antibodies.
Focal seizure, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, diffuse EEG slowing and CSF pleocytosis with oligoclonal bands.
One-week course after HSV encephalitis, no new cortical or deep gray matter diffusion restriction and no periodic sharp-wave complexes on EEG.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced encephalopathy or neuroleptic malignant / serotonin syndrome
differential.key_features: No neuroleptic or serotonergic exposure, toxicology negative, temperature 37.8 C and CK 186 U/L.

key_clinical_evidence: One week of paranoia, aggression and insomnia, incoherent paraphasic speech, a focal motor seizure, orofacial and choreiform dyskinesias and autonomic instability, 2 months after HSV-1 encephalitis: five of the six Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:32) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive 1:10 is read with the CSF.

CSF HSV-1/2 PCR negative and an MRI with only chronic left frontotemporal encephalomalacia, unchanged and without new restricted diffusion, enhancement or hemorrhage, exclude HSV relapse: this is post-HSV autoimmune encephalitis, which follows about a quarter of HSV encephalitis cases, most with NMDAR antibodies (Armangue 2018).

EEG shows left-predominant diffuse slowing, FIRDA and rare left temporal sharp waves; continuous EEG captures two subclinical left temporal seizures and an extreme delta brush-like pattern, which supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Contrast CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis shows no tumor; post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis is not tumor-associated, so treatment is immunotherapy without tumor removal.
Earlier immunotherapy is associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013); here it starts once the CSF HSV PCR excludes viral relapse.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A focal seizure, orofacial and choreiform dyskinesias and autonomic instability accompany the behavioral change; with CSF inflammation they require autoimmune encephalitis to be excluded before the change is attributed to a psychiatric disorder or to sequelae.
red_herrings.data_point: New paranoia, aggression, insomnia and incoherent speech in a 63-year-old man with cognitive deficits after HSV encephalitis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on late-onset psychosis, delirium or behavioral sequelae of the prior encephalitis and delays CSF antibody testing.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing instead of the neurological work-up.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Relapsing symptoms weeks after HSV encephalitis are often autoimmune rather than viral: a negative CSF HSV PCR and an MRI without new lesions exclude HSV relapse, and post-HSV anti-NMDAR encephalitis responds to immunotherapy.
red_herrings.data_point: HSV-1 encephalitis 2 months ago, now with a new seizure, recurrent encephalopathy and temperature 37.8 C.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent to diagnose HSV relapse and continue antivirals alone, or to withhold immunotherapy because of the recent infection.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A parent's late-onset Alzheimer disease does not explain a one-week illness with seizures, dyskinesias and dysautonomia.
red_herrings.data_point: Mother: Alzheimer disease, diagnosed at age 78.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts amyloid imaging or a neurodegenerative framing of the cognitive decline.

metadata.difficulty_description: Diagnostic puzzle: presentation occurs in an atypical demographic (older man) 2 months after HSV-1 encephalitis, mimicking HSV relapse or post-infectious sequelae. MRI shows only chronic changes, routine EEG shows non-specific slowing, and CSF is only mildly abnormal. The decisive result (CSF anti-NMDAR antibodies) must be specifically requested in the CSF order. Distractors include the mother's Alzheimer history, cardiovascular comorbidities, levetiracetam behavioral effects and the temptation to attribute symptoms to residual HSV damage.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required criteria, 4 red herrings, subtype=RP; requires CSF antibody confirmation + MRI/EEG/labs synthesis; dysautonomia demanding ICU-level care; reverse/mimic case with comorbidity and atypical demographic that raise competing differential weight
metadata.revision_reason: Independent Reviewer 2 anti-NMDAR audit: tumour screening tailored by age/sex and moved out of lab payloads; paired serum/CSF anti-GluN1 reachable; routine EEG baseline with selected continuous escalation; blanket CAP CT, FDG-PET and blood cultures removed

patient.history_present_illness: This 63-year-old right-handed man with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and HSV-1 encephalitis 2 months ago presents to the emergency department with worsening confusion and new-onset aggressive, erratic behavior over the past week. His wife reports that following his discharge from inpatient rehabilitation 4 weeks ago, he had persistent mild cognitive deficits and word-finding difficulty, which were attributed to residual effects of his encephalitis. He was making slow but steady progress with outpatient speech therapy and occupational therapy. Approximately one week ago, his wife noticed he became increasingly irritable and suspicious, accusing her of hiding his belongings and conspiring against him. Over the ensuing days, he developed insomnia, refusing to sleep and pacing the house at night. He began speaking incoherently, mixing up words and making statements that did not make contextual sense. Two days prior to presentation, he became physically aggressive, pushing his wife when she attempted to give him his medications, and was found wandering outside the house in his pajamas at 3 AM. On the day of presentation, he had a witnessed episode of rhythmic jerking of the right arm lasting approximately 30 seconds, followed by staring and unresponsiveness for several minutes. Emergency medical services were called and he was brought to the ED. The wife is particularly concerned because his current presentation feels different from his initial encephalitis episode two months ago, which was characterized primarily by somnolence and confusion rather than aggression and paranoia. She denies any recent fevers, headache complaints, neck stiffness, or new medication changes. She notes he has been compliant with his levetiracetam and other home medications. There have been no recent sick contacts, travel, or known toxic exposures.

neurological_exam.additional: Autonomic instability noted: episodic tachycardia to 120s with blood pressure fluctuations (systolic ranging 100-170 mmHg over the past 6 hours). Two brief episodes of diaphoresis. No meningismus. Kernig and Brudzinski signs negative.
neurological_exam.coordination: Unable to reliably assess finger-to-nose or heel-to-shin due to agitation and inability to follow commands.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 3mm bilaterally, reactive to light. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact to light touch bilaterally. Mild right lower facial droop (residual from prior encephalitis). Gag reflex intact. Tongue midline. Intermittent orofacial dyskinesias with lip-smacking and jaw movements noted during examination.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to assess safely due to agitation and combativeness. Per nursing, was ambulatory with unsteady gait prior to acute behavioral decompensation.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but agitated and intermittently combative. Oriented to self only; disoriented to place, time, and situation. Unable to follow multi-step commands. Speech is fluent but with frequent paraphasic errors and tangential content. Montreal Cognitive Assessment attempted but patient unable to cooperate. Exhibits paranoid ideation, stating staff are trying to poison him. Intermittent periods of catatonic-like staring lasting 10-20 seconds.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone increased in bilateral upper extremities with intermittent cogwheel-like rigidity. Strength 4+/5 in right upper and lower extremities (baseline from prior illness), 5/5 on left. No pronator drift on left. Right-sided drift present (known residual). Intermittent choreiform movements of bilateral hands noted.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally. Triceps 2+ bilaterally. Brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally. Patellar 3+ bilaterally (mildly brisk). Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Withdraws to noxious stimuli in all extremities. Detailed sensory examination limited by patient cooperation. Light touch appears grossly intact bilaterally.
